title: The ghost in the machine: Simulation and the future of AI-powered determination
gist: Behavioral simulation - querying synthetically generated populations instead of human panels - is already a paying enterprise category with some buyers spending seven figures a year, attacking a $140B market research industry whose survey answers correlate only ~40% with real behavior. Vendors split into interview-grounded builders (Simile, Rehearsals) and data-rebuilt ones (Aaru, Artificial Societies), but personas, pipelines and query engines will commoditize, leaving first-party calibration data, workflow embedding and validated institutional trust as the moats.

insights.claim: Market research is a $140 billion industry where a single concept test from a large research firm starts in the high five figures and takes weeks, while deeper projects cross into millions and take months.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Sizes the incumbent spend pool that synthetic-population vendors are attacking on both price and cycle time.
insights.locator: The growing demand for synthetic research

insights.claim: Survey and focus-group answers are a weak proxy for behavior: some studies find respondents' answers correlate only about 40% with their subsequent behavior, because conventional studies rest on what people say rather than what they do.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Sets a low incumbent accuracy bar that simulation only has to beat, not perfection - reframes the buyer's hurdle rate.
insights.quote: some studies find their answers correlate only about 40% with their subsequent behavior
insights.locator: The deeper problem goes beyond just cost

insights.claim: High cost forces organizations to selectively limit research to a few key decisions, so the binding constraint on enterprise decision quality is research budget rationing rather than analytical capability.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: The TAM is not the existing $140B of studies but the far larger set of decisions currently made without any research.
insights.locator: A single concept test from a large research firm

insights.claim: The hardest populations to reach - policy insiders, CISOs, orphan populations - are nearly impossible to find and study at all with legacy methodology, leaving entire high-value segments unresearched.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Points to the highest-margin beachhead wedges for simulation vendors: audiences incumbents structurally cannot panel.
insights.locator: The hardest populations to reach

insights.claim: When decisions that would never have justified a strategy consulting engagement can be queried against a synthetic population in an afternoon, the surface area of what deserves to be researched grows exponentially.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Implies demand elasticity, not share-shift - watch for expansion revenue rather than displacement of incumbent research line items.
insights.locator: When decisions that would have never justified

insights.claim: Behavioral simulation followed a compressed adoption curve: LLMs made simulating coherent human reasoning affordable in late 2023, academic papers followed, techniques reached commercial research by 2024, and real enterprise revenue was flowing by 2025.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A two-year lab-to-revenue path means the category is past proof-of-concept risk and into land-grab timing.
insights.locator: Once LLMs made it possible to simulate coherent human reasoning

insights.claim: Some leading enterprises are already spending seven figures annually with emerging population-simulation companies, indicating budgets have shifted from experiment lines to real procurement.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Seven-figure ACVs this early support venture-scale outcomes and justify aggressive entry valuations in the category.
insights.locator: As a result, some leading enterprises are now spending seven figures

insights.claim: Behavioral simulation may be one of the most consequential applied AI use cases to emerge, with the potential to become the layer that enterprises run every meaningful decision through.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Frames the category as a horizontal decision layer rather than a market-research point tool - a much larger prize if it holds.
insights.quote: this technology has the potential to become the layer that enterprises run every meaningful decision through
insights.locator: Behavioral simulation may be one of the most consequential

insights.claim: Real deployments already span consumer packaging tests against 10,000 simulated consumers overnight, political message testing across three swing districts, and NATO-analyst modeling of how 5.1 million people in a European country would respond to a foreign disinformation campaign.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Shows the category already crossing from CPG research into defense and political influence - a stickier and more regulated buyer set.
insights.locator: Consider this: A CMO at a Fortune 500 brand

themes.theme: Two camps: interview-first vs data-first populations

insights.claim: Synthetic-population builders are coalescing into two camps: one grounds populations in real human interviews enriched with behavioral data, the other rebuilds populations purely from ingested sources like census data, behavioral traces, historical panels, and social listening.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Gives a clean diligence axis for comparing startups in the space and predicting which enterprise use cases each can serve.
insights.locator: Market players are coalescing around two primary camps

insights.claim: Simile, a Stanford spinout from the 'Smallville' generative agents study, has moved away from prompting off-the-shelf models toward training proprietary simulation and confidence models that encode behavioral and interview data in the model weights rather than only the context window.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Weight-level encoding is a costlier but more defensible technical posture than prompt-wrapping - a differentiator to test in diligence.
insights.locator: Simile is a Stanford spinout

insights.claim: Simile splits its architecture into an individual model that maintains internal logic for a person's preferences, biases, and worldviews, and a population model that applies those learnings at scale.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: The individual/population split is an emerging reference architecture rivals will be measured against.
insights.locator: Simile has an individual model

insights.claim: Aaru argues that relying only on non-interview data delivers faster time to value and avoids letting the interview itself become a contaminant, because self-reporting imports the very biases that simulation is meant to eliminate.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: If Aaru is right, interview-grounded competitors carry a structural accuracy defect that scales with their data moat.
insights.locator: Aaru is an expression of this philosophy

insights.claim: The interview-based camp counters that using only data and behavioral traces makes validation and backtesting almost impossible, and that calibrating against real, named individuals is what separates a believable twin from a generic persona.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Validation tractability, not raw data volume, may decide which camp survives enterprise procurement.
insights.locator: The interview-based methodology rebuts

insights.claim: The camp boundary is already blurring - interview-first players fold in public data, data-only players absorb clients' first-party surveys and interviews, and hybrids like Electric Twin have emerged - suggesting methodology alone will not be a durable differentiator.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Bet on distribution and data access rather than methodological purity when picking winners here.
insights.locator: That being said, the line can get blurry between camps

insights.claim: Whichever population-construction approach a simulation company starts with reveals its founders' beliefs about where the value lives, and that belief shapes its initial ICP and future roadmap.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Use methodology choice as a leading indicator of a startup's go-to-market and eventual product surface.
insights.quote: Whichever approach a company starts with reveals its founders' beliefs about where the value lives
insights.locator: Whichever approach a company starts with

insights.claim: Population simulation is a distinct route from AI-native qualitative interviewing platforms such as Strella and Listen Labs, which automate conversations with real respondents rather than modeling behavior and generating synthetic populations.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Prevents mis-comping two categories with different unit economics and defensibility profiles.
insights.locator: A related category of AI-native platforms

insights.claim: Enterprise simulation accuracy should be judged on three ascending tiers: attitude replication (matching what people say), behavioral replication (matching what people do under changing conditions), and emergent simulation (staying accurate on inputs outside the training or interview data).
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A ready-made diligence rubric: ask which tier a vendor's published accuracy figure actually measures.
insights.locator: three tiers of accuracy

insights.claim: Most published accuracy figures in the behavioral-simulation category only measure attitude replication, whose ceiling is set by surveys and benchmarks that correlate weakly with actual behavior.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Treat headline accuracy claims as near-meaningless marketing unless the evaluation is behavioral and out-of-sample.
insights.locator: This is what most published figures measure

insights.claim: Behavioral replication has only scattered evidence and rigorous out-of-sample evaluation is rare, yet buyer benchmarks suggest the best simulation products land within 10-15% of actual campaign outcomes - good enough to drive real commercial decisions.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: The 10-15% error band is the concrete number to hold vendors to when validating claims.
insights.quote: Buyer benchmarks suggest the best products land within 10–15% of actual campaign outcomes, good enough to drive real commercial decisions.
insights.locator: Behavioral replication

insights.claim: The real test of emergent simulation is whether agent-to-agent interaction reproduces macro phenomena no individual agent could - sentiment indices, retail trends, or electoral outcomes.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Emergence is the capability that would extend these platforms into macro forecasting and market-level prediction.
insights.locator: Emergent simulation

insights.claim: Even directional accuracy from a synthetic population is commercially valuable for narrowing choice sets and pre-filtering ideas before expensive human research, since the realistic alternative is the rough guesses decision-makers rely on today.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Adoption does not require solving accuracy - vendors can monetize as a cheap pre-filter layer well before parity.
insights.locator: However, even directional accuracy can be valuable

insights.claim: If simulation outputs are unverifiable or untraceable, buyers will lack confidence in the results and the category may not survive serious procurement or renewal.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Traceability tooling is a survival requirement, not a feature - watch renewal rates as the category's real health metric.
insights.locator: Accuracy is the first checkpoint

insights.claim: Enterprise buyers of population simulation are methodologically agnostic, routinely evaluating products from both camps and deciding on specific use cases and technical requirements rather than a provider's philosophy of population construction.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Vendor differentiation pitched on methodology will not convert; expect competition to resolve on use-case fit and integration.
insights.locator: While startups have varied across both camps

themes.theme: Where the moats are and aren't

insights.claim: Synthetic personas, data pipelines, and the query engine are not where moats lie in behavioral simulation, because foundation models and public data will likely commoditize all three within a few years.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Discount valuations built on persona or pipeline IP; the technical layer is a depreciating asset.
insights.quote: we don't view synthetic personas, the data pipelines, or the query engine as where the moats lie
insights.locator: What the winners will need to get right

insights.claim: The durable moats in behavioral simulation will be proprietary first-party data that calibrates each population, the workflows the product embeds into, and institutional trust earned through rigorous validation.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Underwrite deals on customer data access and workflow depth, not model quality.
insights.locator: We believe the real moats will be

insights.claim: Each enterprise simulation deployment feeds response data back into the system, sharpening the next prediction and compounding into proprietary signal - a flywheel that rewards early enterprise logos disproportionately.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Early logo count is a leading indicator of eventual accuracy lead; late entrants face a compounding deficit.
insights.locator: The data flywheel

insights.claim: Population construction, not query speed, is where simulation accuracy is won or lost, because a query run against a poorly assembled population is fast and wrong.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Diligence should probe calibration and composition craft rather than demo latency or UI polish.
insights.quote: A query run against a poorly assembled population is fast and wrong, so composition and calibration are where accuracy is won or lost.
insights.locator: Constructing that population is where the craft lives

insights.claim: A simulation product becomes structurally sticky only when it stops being a one-off consultation and becomes a fixed step in every launch, pricing call, and campaign, at which point removing it means rebuilding part of the organization's decision-making process.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Track usage frequency per account as the churn predictor - episodic usage signals a fragile contract.
insights.locator: The product workflow

insights.claim: Institutional trust in a simulation provider is slow to build but, once predictions hold up across engagements and customers can defend decisions by pointing to how the system reached them, it makes that provider difficult to dislodge.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Expect a long land phase and winner-take-most dynamics per account; incumbency will be hard to displace after the first renewals.
insights.locator: Institutional trust

insights.claim: A separate emerging category, including Mantic and Preseen, predicts discrete event outcomes such as election results, supply chain disruption probability, and regulatory decisions, with many founders getting their start on Metaculus leaderboards or betting in prediction markets.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A distinct investable lane adjacent to behavioral simulation, with an unusually legible talent signal in public forecasting track records.
insights.locator: Separately, while we have focused on simulation of human behavior

insights.claim: Nothing stops a state from running behavioral simulations for political targeting or propaganda optimization, and no one has answered who owns the responses of a live person's digital twin once it becomes accurate enough to query in their absence.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Unresolved consent and ownership questions are the category's main regulatory tail risk - a plausible trigger for legislation that reprices these assets.
insights.quote: no one has answered who owns the responses of a live person's digital twin once it becomes accurate enough to query in their absence
insights.locator: As technical capabilities evolve, the need for commercial and ethical boundaries grows

insights.claim: The synthetic-population category is still in its early innings and companies need time to earn enterprise trust and test their simulations against real world outcomes, meaning current accuracy claims outrun verified evidence.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Expect a shakeout as validation catches up; favor vendors publishing out-of-sample results over those publishing benchmarks.
insights.locator: The category is still in its early innings
